evidence: One reference with public numbers (2,166,790 views, 23,825 likes, about 2,392 comments, about 24,000 subscribers, as of 2026-11-25): these are what the reference does, not proof of what performs. No result evidence. Ranged values are the reference's single figure widened about 15% either way; single values are limits or facts as measured. Format and length follow the brief (vertical 1080x1920, no longer than 60 s), not the reference (horizontal 1920x1080, 537.2 s). The reference has no voice, so spoken-word values are null and the word budget is the analyst's count of on-screen text. Tool figures are as measured over the full 537.2 s; what they come to in a 60 s film is in notes.scaled_to_60s and is arithmetic, not measurement.

hook.type: cold open on the scenario's far end: the most extreme picture of the first half, with two counters already disagreeing (a year in the billions against five minutes) and one flat second-person sentence stating the small number
hook.question_opened: how did five minutes of standing still put you here, and where does it stop?

structure.does: 0.13-5.5 s: cold open on the far end of the scenario (the film's own 312-318 s), both counters at extreme values, one 8-word second-person line
6.5-10.3 s: the ordinary starting scene at 0 seconds; the title as a question, centred, on 3.4 s. Opens the central question

10.3-44 s: the first visible symptom (picture first, then a 5-word line), the rule stated once (you are normal, the world is fast), the rate said in words, then seconds to minutes to hours to days, each with one new visible change
44-116 s: days blur, seasons, years, decades, centuries. Two lines measure it against people (ten years older; everyone you met is gone). A thread opened at 62.5 s closes at 91.1 s
116-319 s: forest, ice, canyon, mountains, desert, bare rock, a galaxy overhead. The ground colour changes with each stage. The cold-open picture is reached at 312-318 s (0.58)
319-505 s: no ground, no galaxies, no stars, one black hole. The frame is near-black from 344 s. Slowest part of the film (see notes)
505.5 s one white flash; 506.9 s a 9-word final line; the countdown row reads NOTHING / ever. Preceded by a 7.0 s gap with no line
510.7-521 s: three lines on black; sound about 12 dB down; a click every second; the viewer's watch comes back into frame
521.9 s a one-word turn; 524.5 s a warm dot; 527.7 s it is the street light from 25 s; opening scene back by 531 s; outside clock resets and starts to speed up again; file ends in motion

left_block_rows: small caps label for the outside quantity
small caps rate row: one second for you = current rate
NEXT row: the coming event in 2-4 words with a countdown in outside time
right_block_rows: small caps label: how long you have been standing here
large serif figure running at real time, never reset
small caps comparison: outside time elapsed put in human terms

share_triggers: evidence: a final line that can be quoted alone, 506.9 s (comment ranks 3 and 10; 2,200 likes on rank 3)
evidence: the return to the opening scene after the bleakest moment, 521.9-537 s (rank 43 with timestamp 8:45, 548 likes; ranks 34, 19, 25)
evidence: one strong early picture, the Sun as a stripe at 40.7 s (rank 57, timestamp 0:41, 742 likes)
evidence: viewers apply it to their own lives though the film never does (rank 1, 4,700 likes; rank 86, hearted by the uploader)
evidence: a premise a fandom already has a name for (32 of the top 100 comments, 48% of their likes); a property of the topic, not of the craft
guess: sending it says 'this is how fast it goes', a feeling, not a fact
comment_triggers: evidence: second person makes the viewer a character and people finish the story (15 of top 100 comments, 17% of likes)
evidence: short flat final lines are quoted or answered (8 comments; lines at 87, 91, 171, 283, 407, 506.9 s and one counter comparison)
evidence: a recognisable premise draws in-jokes (32 comments, 48% of likes)
evidence: the loop and small details at the end are pointed out and explained (ranks 34, 19, 26, 48)
evidence: single strong moments get timestamps (8 comments: 0:30-0:37, 0:41, 2:07, 2:51, 3:28, 4:43, 8:40, 8:45)
evidence: the film asks the viewer nothing: no question, no call to comment, no disputed claim
do not copy: a continuity slip drew a correction (trees at 3:28, 396 likes); 6 comments call the look machine-made

sound.music: character not measurable. A continuous low bed: at least 85% of energy below 250 Hz in every 20 s window, steady components at 49 and 98 Hz, a regular swell about every 0.41-0.45 s from 24 s to about 524 s

look.accent_means: warm light: the sunset, the molten ground, the black hole's disc, and the street light that is the last thing seen
look.style: one continuous first-person 3D scene: flat-shaded low-polygon solids on the ground, soft glowing sky; two counter blocks in the top corners; one italic serif line at the bottom

brightness_arc.what: mid-tone: sunset street, then one ground colour per stage
near-black space; the text is the brightest thing in frame
the opening scene again (0.33 is the opening chapter's mean; the last 7 s were not measured separately)

type.faces: a serif with a true italic (figures, title, story lines); a wide-tracked sans in capitals (labels). Not identified by name

look.camera: fixed position, slow turning throughout; turns and tilts on cue from a line; looks down at the viewer's own body

notes.format.duration_s: The brief: about one minute and no longer than 60 seconds. 60 is the hard upper limit; 55 is the analyst's reading of 'about one minute'. The reference runs 537.2 s.
notes.format.fps: The reference is 30 fps; the brief does not set a rate.
notes.hook.first_word_s: null: the reference has no voice. transcribe.py found no speech; a second pass without its voice filter on five windows found none.
notes.hook.words_in_first_3s: null for spoken words. On screen there are 8 words in the line and about 29 words and figures in the two counter blocks (analyst's count).
notes.hook.first_picture_s: Tool figure. The reference opens on a black frame and fades up by 0.4 s. That is a fault (breakdown section 10, item 1): our film should have its picture and line on the first frame.
notes.hook.first_cut_s: Tool figure, and an artefact: 0.233 s is the fade up from black, not a cut. The first real scene change is a dip through black at 5.5-6.5 s. compare.py will hold our first cut to 0.6 s (pass) or 0.97 s (warn). A film that opens on full picture, as it should, will only meet that if something in the scene flips inside the first half second; otherwise read that row as an artefact of the reference's fade, not as a defect in ours.
notes.pacing.words_per_minute: null: no spoken words. The writer's word budget comes from on_screen_words_per_minute: 105 measured (944 words in 537.2 s: 928 in 139 story lines, 8 in the cold-open line, 8 in the title), widened 15%. Analyst's count from contact sheets.
notes.pacing.speaking_rate_wpm: null: no voice. If the producer adds none, there is no voice speed to set.
notes.pacing.line_start_to_start_s: Measured mean 3.79 s, median 3.80 s, range 2.6-9.2 s (analyst's detector at 10 frames a second, checked by eye). The reference keeps almost exactly this interval from 95 s to 483 s; that uniformity is a fault (section 10, item 7). Match the average, vary the gaps.
notes.pacing.line_on_screen_s: Measured about 2.6 s including 0.2-0.3 s fades, the same for 1-word and 12-word lines. The sameness is a fault (section 10, item 6): time each line by its length, at about 2.6 words a second (the reference's average load), with about 1.4 s as the shortest.
notes.pacing.mean_shot_s: Tool figure 7.67 s widened 15%. The tool's 70 'shots' are not edits: by eye the film has no edit cuts, one dip through black and one fade up from black. The tool is counting the world flipping state (day to night, grass to snow, ice arriving). Kept as the tool's figure because the tool will count our flips the same way.
notes.pacing.cuts_per_10s: Tool figure 1.28 widened 15%. It is an average over a film whose last five minutes have almost no flips. The reference's own first 60 s measures 3.17 per 10 s (pacing.first_60s_of_reference, from the same measure.json, windowed by the analyst). A 60 s film that flips as often as the reference's opening will sit near 3 and show above the band in compare.py; that is the like-for-like comparison and should not be read as too fast.
notes.pacing.longest_shot_s: Tool figure 108.03 s (189.5-297.5 s). A 60 s film cannot reach compare.py's band for this row (70 s or more to pass). Expect a fail on 'longest shot' by construction.
notes.pacing.longest_still_s: Tool figure. The picture is never frozen because both counters change every frame. Ours must do the same or it will read as frozen.
notes.pacing.end_hold_s: Tool figure 0.0 s. The film ends in motion as the opening scene starts to speed up again. This is the ending's design, not a fault; compare.py passes an end hold up to 0.3 s.
notes.pacing.payoff_at_share_of_run: Measured: payoff picture at 505.5 s, payoff line at 506.9 s, of 537.2 s. The cold open's promise is met earlier, at 312-318 s (0.58). See scaled_to_60s for why 0.94 does not carry over.
notes.structure: Shares are of the reference's 537.2 s. The slowest stretch is 437-496 s (tool motion under 0.3 for 77 s; one ring on black) at 0.81-0.92 of the run. That is a fault (section 10, item 8), not a role to reproduce.
notes.sound.integrated_lufs: Tool figure. It is 7.4 LU under the -14 LUFS YouTube plays loud videos at, and is listed as a possible fault (section 10, item 14); whether it was deliberate cannot be known. compare.py passes loudness within 1.5 LU of this figure, so a louder master will show as a difference on that row. That is a decision for the producer, not something to settle here.
notes.sound.music: The analyst cannot hear the file. Frequencies and periods are measured; mood, instrument and whether this is music or designed noise are not measurable.
notes.sound.cuts_on_sound_share: Tool figure. With 2.88 onsets a second, chance gives 0.37 for hard cuts and 0.82 for gradual ones, so 0.652 is not evidence of deliberate sync. compare.py passes at 0.50 or more.
notes.sound.onsets_per_s: Tool figure. With no voice, these come from the pulsing bed. compare.py passes 1.5 to 4.2; a bed with no pulse and no events will fall below.
notes.sound.payoff_drop_db: Per-second level falls from about -22 to about -33 dBFS across 508-511 s and returns across 521-524 s (analyst's measurement). Nine clicks 1.00 s apart at 515.0-523.0 s.
notes.look.ground: Tool figure for the whole run, pulled dark by the 34% of the film that is near-black space. The opening is a mid-tone sunset. compare.py compares our whole-run ground, brightness (0.23) and dark share (0.58) with these, so a film with a shorter dark part will measure brighter. See look.brightness_arc and scaled_to_60s.
notes.look.stage_grounds: Median colour of a ground box sampled once a second in each chapter (analyst's measurement), except snow, which is by eye and has no hex. They are the reference's stages; ours will have its own.
notes.look.type: Estimates from full-size stills at 1080 high. The small label size is a fault (section 10, item 4), given so that it is not repeated. Shares are of the horizontal frame's height and do not transfer directly to a vertical frame.
notes.counters: Counts are from the analyst's samples (one frame per story line plus sheets); a short-lived state between samples could be missed, so read 27 and 12 as 'at least'.

scaled_to_60s.basis: Arithmetic from the reference's measured figures and the brief's 60 s limit. The reference does not show any of this.
scaled_to_60s.alternative: 4 stages of about 11 s with 3 lines each
scaled_to_60s.why_stage_length: The reference's shortest chapter is 8 s with 2 lines (44-52 s); the steps in its first minute run 3 to 10 s each.
scaled_to_60s.why_lines: 60 s at one line per 3.79 s is 15.8; allowing longer holds for longer lines and one long gap gives 13. The reference's own first 60 s has 15 story lines plus the cold-open line and the title.
scaled_to_60s.words_per_line: aim at the reference's mean of 6.7 or under; 8 at most. Its 10-12 word lines do not fit one row of a vertical frame at a readable size (analyst's estimate: 5 or 6 words a row).
scaled_to_60s.line_on_screen_s: words divided by 2.6, and not under 1.4
scaled_to_60s.why_payoff: The reference's 0.94 leaves 31.7 s after the payoff. 0.94 of 60 s leaves 3.6 s, not enough for an aftermath line, a turn and a return at about 2.6 s a line.
scaled_to_60s.brightness: In proportion the reference would be mid-tone to about 38 s, near-black from about 38 s to 59 s and back to the opening for the last second. The return needs 4 to 5 s to read, so the dark part must end earlier than that.
scaled_to_60s.layout: The two counter blocks side by side at the reference's size come to about 1,100 px against a 1,080 px frame. They need a new layout for vertical; the reference does not show one.
